desc: The founding document of the modern disclosure record. Filed 25 May 2022 with the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community by Irvin Charles McCullough III - the IC's first Inspector General - on behalf of David Grusch, under Presidential Policy Directive 19 and the urgent-concern statute. It followed an earlier July 2021 protected disclosure by Grusch to the DoD Inspector General. The preponderance of the complaint is classified; Grusch's unclassified characterization under oath is that it concerns 'both material acquisition and exploitation activity' and the withholding of UAP baselining data from the intelligence professionals who brief aircrews. In July 2022 the ICIG determined the complaint credible and urgent, the statutory trigger for transmission to the congressional intelligence committees. A companion reprisal complaint alleges Grusch's identity and his UAP communications with the DoD IG were disclosed outside the IG channel; the unclassified version reported in June 2023 names Avril Haines, Sean Kirkpatrick, Susan Gough, Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand and Rep. Tim Burchett in its account of how the information moved. Grusch testified that the ICIG had no smooth mechanism to route the disclosure to the Armed Services Committees despite Title 10 equities - meaning the substantive Title 10 allegations may never have reached the committees with jurisdiction over the alleged programs.

entityInfo.desc: Chain of custody for the complaint, as established by sworn testimony and reporting. July 2021: Grusch makes a protected disclosure of classified information to the DoD Inspector General concerning the improper withholding and concealment of UAP-related material from Congress. 25 May 2022: Irvin Charles McCullough III of Compass Rose Legal Group, the first Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, files a PPD-19 urgent-concern complaint with the ICIG on Grusch's behalf. July 2022: the ICIG determines the complaint credible and urgent, the statutory trigger for transmission to the congressional intelligence committees. A companion reprisal complaint alleges Grusch's identity and his DoD IG communications were disclosed to DoD and IC entities outside the IG's office; the unclassified version reported in June 2023 references DNI Avril Haines, AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick, DoD spokesperson Susan Gough, Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand and Rep. Tim Burchett in its account of how the information moved. Grusch's unclassified description of the underlying subject matter, given under oath to Chairman Grothman: 'Both material acquisition and exploitation activity, also baselining the UAPs but not sharing it with, you know, intelligence professionals that are actually doing step briefs to pilots.' He further testified that the preponderance of the complaint was classified, that he knows the exact locations of held material and provided them to the Inspector General and in part to the intelligence committees, and that he had the individuals with firsthand knowledge make their own protected disclosures. He also testified to a routing failure: PPD-19 and ICD 120 send such disclosures to the intelligence committees, and there was no good mechanism for the ICIG to provide his information to the House and Senate Armed Services Committees despite Title 10 equities being at play.
